skill.name: react-native-best-practices
skill.description: Guides React Native performance analysis and optimization for frame rate, startup time, bundle size, memory, rerenders, and animations. Covers Hermes, Expo, profiling tools, native modules, threading, lists, and release validation.
skill.summary: Measure, diagnose, and improve React Native performance across JavaScript, iOS, Android, Hermes, Expo, and application bundles.
skill.author: callstackincubator

content.value_statement: React Native apps can suffer from slow startup, dropped frames, excessive rerenders, memory growth, and oversized bundles. This skill guides measurement, diagnosis, targeted optimization, and validation across JavaScript, iOS, Android, Hermes, and Expo.
actual_capabilities: Guides profiling with React DevTools, agent-device, Xcode Instruments, Android Studio, Flashlight, and bundle analyzers.
Diagnoses list scrolling, rerenders, animations, bottom sheets, TextInput responsiveness, memory growth, and JavaScript thread stalls.
Recommends bundle analysis, import cleanup, tree shaking, R8, asset optimization, dependency review, and guarded code splitting.
Explains startup measurement, Hermes memory mapping, cold-start markers, native navigation, and screen preloading.
Provides native module, threading, ownership, lifecycle, view flattening, and Android alignment guidance.
limitations: The skill provides guidance but does not collect benchmarks or profiler traces without project access and suitable tools.
Recommendations depend on React Native, Expo, architecture, and library versions.
Local commands can create build artifacts or change dependencies and require review before execution.
Third-party profilers, analyzers, and libraries require separate installation, configuration, and supply-chain review.

use_cases.title: Fix a Slow Screen
use_cases.description: Profile a laggy interaction, identify rerender or list bottlenecks, and validate a focused change.

use_cases.title: Reduce Startup and Bundle Cost
use_cases.description: Measure cold startup and package size, then prioritize Hermes, bundling, asset, and native optimizations.

use_cases.title: Review Performance Regressions
use_cases.description: Compare evidence across releases and produce a ranked remediation plan with validation criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React Native screen for obvious performance risks. Use the provided code and project versions. Prioritize three changes and explain how to measure each.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one screen or component.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Frame Drops
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose frame drops during [interaction]. Use these profiler results: [metrics]. Identify likely causes, request missing evidence, and propose a measure-change-remeasure sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Startup and Bundles
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a startup and bundle optimization plan for this React Native [version] app using [Hermes or JSC]. Compare baseline metrics and rank changes by impact and risk.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across startup and release artifacts.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this regression across JavaScript, native threads, memory, and bundle delivery. Correlate [trace], [render profile], and [build data]. Recommend minimal fixes with validation and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: A product list drops to 42 FPS while scrolling.
output: Finding: render profiling shows repeated item updates during scrolling.
Recommendation: stabilize item props and use a suitable virtualized list.
Validation: repeat the interaction and compare frame rate and rerender counts.

output_examples.input: Cold startup takes 3.4 seconds on Android with Hermes.
output: Finding: startup markers separate native initialization, bundle loading, and first meaningful render.
Recommendation: address the largest measured phase before adding speculative preloading.
Validation: compare multiple cold starts on the same release device.

output_examples.input: The release application grew after adding several libraries.
output: Finding: bundle and application-size reports identify the largest new JavaScript, native, and asset contributors.
Recommendation: remove unused imports, compare dependency alternatives, and verify R8 and asset settings.
Validation: rebuild the same release variant and compare download and install sizes.

best_practices: Capture a repeatable baseline before changing code, then repeat the same interaction after each change.
Confirm React Native and library versions before applying version-specific guidance.
Review local commands and dependency changes before execution, especially release builds and third-party profiling tools.
anti_patterns: Do not recommend memoization, state rewrites, or compiler changes without measured rerender or frame-rate evidence.
Do not apply every optimization simultaneously because results become difficult to attribute and regressions become harder to isolate.
Do not load remote JavaScript chunks from user-controlled or untrusted origins.

faq.question: What performance areas does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers frame rate, rerenders, startup time, bundles, application size, memory, animations, lists, TextInput, native modules, and threading.

faq.question: Does it support Expo projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Expo-specific bundle analysis, tree-shaking, prebuild, and profiling guidance where the project version supports those workflows.

faq.question: Does it modify my project automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends targeted changes and commands. Review each change and run it through your normal development workflow.

faq.question: Which measurements should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a repeatable interaction, device details, build type, project versions, baseline metrics, profiler output, and recent relevant changes.

faq.question: Can it diagnose native performance issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Xcode Instruments, Android Studio Profiler, native threading, memory ownership, Turbo Modules, view hierarchies, and alignment.

faq.question: Are remote chunks recommended for bundle reduction?
faq.answer: Only for existing or explicit remote-code architectures. Use first-party signed artifacts, trusted HTTPS origins, fixed manifests, and strict verification.
